maya: bringing up hf/ornith-12b on dedicated — quick heads up: offline evals show token-drop / quality dip around ~1800 tokens, looks like truncation + small attention drift
ishaan: can you paste the model's config.json?
maya: sure, snippet below (from HF repo):
```json
{
  "max_position_embeddings": 2048,
  "num_attention_heads": 128,
  "num_key_value_heads": 64,
  "rope_scaling": {"type": "linear", "factor": 0.5},
  "sliding_window": true,
  "special_tokens_map": {"pad_token": "<|pad|>"}
}
```
dave: ok two obvious red flags: max_position_embeddings > our default 1024 (will truncate if not handled) and num_key_value_heads != num_attention_heads in ways our runtime expects
tina: + rope_scaling and sliding_window are handled differently between HF and Redwood. HF boolean or small dicts, Redwood expects explicit per-layer factors or a normalized rope_scale config. legacy conversion scripts often skip sliding_window params.
ishaan: short triage checklist: 1) cap or expose max_pos to 2048 in runtime (or remap to Redwood "max_position_buffer"); 2) remap num_key_value_heads -> our kv grouping logic (we assume kv_heads == attention_heads / kv_group by default); 3) convert rope_scaling dict -> per-layer scale array; 4) normalize sliding_window: {enabled:false/true, window_size:int}
maya: can you share a quick patch? I have CI running but want a local fix first.
ishaan: here's a tiny conversion shim we use for onboarding (paste):
```python
# hf -> redwood minimal patch
cfg = load_json('config.json')
# max pos handling
if cfg.get('max_position_embeddings', 0) > 1024:
    cfg['runtime_max_position'] = cfg['max_position_embeddings']
    cfg['max_position_embeddings'] = 1024  # keep on-disk compat
# kv heads mapping
if cfg.get('num_key_value_heads'):
    cfg['num_kv_groups'] = cfg['num_attention_heads'] // cfg['num_key_value_heads']
# rope scaling -> per-layer list fallback
rs = cfg.get('rope_scaling')
if isinstance(rs, dict):
    factor = rs.get('factor', 1.0)
    cfg['rope_scale_per_layer'] = [factor] * cfg.get('num_hidden_layers', 1)
# sliding window normalize
if isinstance(cfg.get('sliding_window'), bool):
    cfg['sliding_window'] = {'enabled': cfg['sliding_window'], 'size': 512}
save_json('config_converted.json', cfg)
```
dave: nice. also watch special_tokens_map -> tokenizer.json differences, HF uses <|pad|> vs our tokenizer expecting <pad>. remap via tokenizer.add_special_tokens({"pad_token": "<pad>"})
maya: ran the shim locally against the model repo — short report:
- setting runtime_max_position=2048 and clamping in config recovered most of the truncation artifacts
- remapping kv groups fixed a ~0.6% perplexity delta but not completely identical to HF outputs
- rope scaling conversion reduced drift but we still see subtle attention score shifts on long contexts
ina: (not in thread) I'd also check whether quantization step was applied after conversion; quantized kernels can amplify small head mismatches.
ishaan: good call — run float32 baseline then int8 quant smoke test. include the same prompt set and log logits/entropy diffs.
onboard-bot: Ticket INF-4123 created: "ornith-12b conversion: max_pos / kv_heads / rope_scaling inconsistencies" (assignee: eng-ml)
ops-bot: noted and added to dedicated-onboard queue. tagging @platform-ops for capacity and runtime flag to expose runtime_max_position :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maya: thanks — running baseline + quant smoke now, will post eval CSV. if we still see head-level deltas we'll try forcing kv_grouping code path in the runtime rather than the conversion shim.
ishaan: if you hit non-deterministic small diffs, dump attention maps for a couple seeds — that'll pinpoint whether mismatch is structural (kv mapping) or numeric (quant/ops).
maya: update (15m): baseline float eval looks back in-line after max_pos clamp; int8 shows ~0.9% BLEU drop on our bench set, digging into kv regrouping next. will follow up in this thread. :mag:
